text:
sara-cs: customer (acme) opened a ticket - their hosted endpoint returned repeated 503s during a streaming toolcall, started ~10:32 UTC. they attached a snippet showing a 500 then 503s. link: https://acme.support/12345

deploy-bot: incident created #INC-2026-0456 (assigned: tim-oncall) :rotating_light:

tim-oncall: thanks — can someone grab the runner logs + dmesg and nvml output? did they include a request id?

lisa-support: request id 9f3a2b in their ticket, sample curl + headers they ran included `Expect: 100-continue` and streaming chunked body.

nishit-ml: quick look at the logs they pasted shows abrupt process exit in the runner: `Signal 11 (SEGV)` from `attn_kern.cu` followed by container restart. also see `CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN` in nvml right before.

jonathan-eng: that smells like a kernel-level crash in the custom attention kernel after a large kv-prefetch. i opened a debug snapshot for the host that served that request.

maria-sre: host dmesg shows: `nvidia: Xid 79` then `OOM in Cuda` and a watchdog reset. suspect GPU driver reset.

eng-infra: we temporarily routed ACME to fallback model variant (cpu-backed small) and cleared backlog, telemetry shows successful retries. rolling that routing now for customers hitting the same request-id pattern.

tim-oncall: steps to reproduce requested — can you paste a minimal reproducer and the exact model + batch size? we need to confirm if this is data-specific or size-specific.

lisa-support: reproducer (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/huge-attn-v1","input":"<long chat>...","stream":true,"tool_call":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
They said it consistently fails when they include a ~180k token context + an embed prefetch call.

nishit-ml: i attached the gdb backtrace from the coredump we captured (short):
```
#0  0x00007fabcde in attn_kern::compute(...)
#1  0x00007fabcd1 in runner::prefetch_kv(...)
#2  0x0000567ab in main_loop()
```
Looks like index arithmetic in attn kernel.

jonathan-eng: low-risk mitigation: disable aggressive kv-prefetch for the model variant on hosted runtime, and force smaller per-request chunking to reduce peak seq len. i'll push a canary to one pool.

maria-sre: Triage notes: - Impact: ACME production requests 10:32-10:40 UTC, ~120 failed requests - Root symptoms: GPU reset (Xid 79) followed by runner segfault - Likely causes: kernel bug with long-context attention + prefetch memory pattern OR driver race under high pinned memory

tim-oncall: next actions: 1) roll canary with kv-prefetch disabled for heavy-context models (jonathan) 2) collect full nvml logs and host kernel logs for 1h around incident (maria) 3) ask ACME to try model with `max_context=65k` to see if it's context size (lisa) 4) open internal bug with kernel repro (nishit)

eng-infra: rolled canary to 10% of traffic targeting same pool. initial 5m looks stable, no Xid after change. will keep monitoring. :thumbsup:

lisa-support: informed customer of temporary routing + ask to try smaller context; they're ok with the workaround for now but request ETA for permanent fix.

nishit-ml: working on a reduced unit test to reproduce the segfault in CI, sharing branch in ~2h. if we get deterministic repro we can file a kernel patch.

tim-oncall: thanks everyone — i'll keep this thread updated. tagging @oncall-followup for postmortem.

maria-sre: added links to collected logs: s3://redwood-incident-logs/7365432100/{nvml.log,runner.log,dmesg.txt}

sara-cs: CS update: ACME acknowledged workaround; asked for ETA and whether billing was affected (they saw retries). i'll escalate billing Qs separately.

tim-oncall: logging this as Sev2 for now, moving to postmortem when stable. closing active escalation if no further 503s in next 2h. :white_check_mark:
